name: 设置 / 平台 SSH 密钥 / 重新生成、拒绝损坏私钥、导入既有私钥并刷新回读

runtime_evidence.reason: The contract ends at the server's own key pair. No node, sshd, agent, container or GPU is claimed.

crud.create: The server seeds the key pair; UI Rotate creates a replacement through POST /ssh-key/rotate
crud.read: Public key, fingerprint and authorize command are shown; reload and independent GET agree
crud.update: UI Import replaces the key through PUT /ssh-key with an unencrypted OpenSSH private key
crud.delete: N/A: no delete operation; the server keeps one platform key

covered: independent GET sees the new key
confirmation title and rotation impact warning are asserted before accepting
corrupt input rejected with the modal open and no key change
fingerprint and public-key blob match ssh-keygen
GET and the page contain no private-key material
reopening the dialog does not echo the submitted private key
missing: cancel and re-open preserving or clearing a non-submitted draft

covered: rendered after load, rotation and import
missing: that the command actually authorizes the key on a real sshd

checklist_items.1.1: The import dialog has one textbox. Its accessible name is the private-key label. It is not marked required. It opens empty, with the OpenSSH private-key header as its placeholder, with no unit and no maximum length, and it stays visible. The import button stays disabled while the text is empty and while it is only whitespace. Reading it and typing that whitespace send no PUT. The import body has only private_key_pem. The independent GET returns authorize_command, created_at, fingerprint, and public_key, and it does not return the private key
checklist_items.1.2: covered: While the SSH key GET is held the import dialog opens with an empty private key and a disabled submit, and the card shows no fingerprint; after the load the generated fingerprint is shown, and a later reload shows the imported fingerprint without echoing the private key
checklist_items.1.7: Rotating the platform SSH key fills no fields. The regenerate control is one dangerous button. Confirming it sends one POST to /api/v1/ssh-key/rotate with an empty body and a 200 response whose fingerprint, public key, and authorize command match the independent GET and differ from the key shown before the rotate. The success sentence is visible. After reload the card shows that same fingerprint and authorize command.
checklist_items.1.11: covered: Cancel, close and Escape each close the import dialog immediately, with no unsaved-changes prompt and no key write, so the stored platform key stays unchanged
checklist_items.1.13: While the import dialog is open on the typed private key, another session's rotate returns 200. The independent GET fingerprint changes. The dialog stays open on that typed key and shows no conflict. The card still shows the previous fingerprint. Saving the import returns success, and the independent GET fingerprint is the imported key, not the other session's fingerprint
checklist_items.1.9: covered: While the import PUT is held a second click and Enter send no further import, and the later success is the only stored key
checklist_items.1.10: Invalid private-key content is rejected without changing the stored key; the modal remains usable and a later valid import succeeds
checklist_items.1.14: Reload and independent GET preserve the rotated and imported key
checklist_items.1.15: Tab from the private key reaches Cancel, then Import once the key is filled. Import can be focused. Enter in the empty key inserts a newline, sends no key PUT, and leaves Import disabled. Enter in the filled key ssh-probe inserts a newline, sends no key PUT, and leaves the dialog open on that value. At 1440×900 the key, Import, and Cancel each stay inside the viewport, and the key does not overlap Import or Cancel.
checklist_items.7.3: N/A: the private key is supplied by the user, not a one-time plaintext credential issued by the platform
checklist_items.7.6: GET and the page contain no private-key material; the import dialog reopens empty; secret-bearing failures omit screenshots and reports are redacted
checklist_items.12.1: covered: Import key on the SSH card opens the dialog named by the import title
checklist_items.12.2: covered: Import dialog at 1440x900: the dialog and footer Import stay inside the viewport, and the title, help text, body and footer sit inside the dialog without overlap
checklist_items.12.3: covered: Default focus is inside the import dialog. Tab and Shift+Tab each cycle across at least two controls and never leave the dialog
checklist_items.12.4: covered: Cancel, Escape, close and mask each return focus to the card Import button and send no PUT
checklist_items.12.5: N/A: the import dialog has no nested child layer
checklist_items.12.6: Rejected import preserves the modal and stored key; successful import is independently read back
checklist_items.12.7: The destructive confirmation is on regenerate rather than delete, and both halves of 12.7 that this component can have are asserted. exercise_ssh_rotate_minimum opens the Popconfirm from the card's only dangerous button and requires it to carry both the confirmation question and the impact sentence - that nodes which only authorized the current key stop accepting the server and lose out-of-band recovery until they authorize the new one - before the POST is allowed. The failure path is asserted too: importing an invalid private key shows the product's importFailed reason, the dialog stays open, and an independent GET proves the fingerprint is still the rotated one, so the rejected attempt left nothing half-applied. Proven by mutation: dropping description={t('sshKey.rotateWarning')} from the Popconfirm in PlatformSSHKeyCard makes the case fail. Reference blocking and allow-with-cleanup have no counterpart here: the platform key is unreferenced and cannot be deleted, only replaced.
checklist_items.12.8: N/A: the platform key has no delete preview, revision or compare-and-swap
checklist_items.16.1: covered for the part that applies: the import is a paste textarea (rows 8) with no file picker, no accept list and no maxlength, so there is no upload type or size boundary to exercise here. What does apply is damaged content, and the case proves it - the literal string 'not a private key' is submitted, the localized import-failed reason appears, the dialog stays open, and an independent GET shows the stored fingerprint is unchanged, so a rejected import cannot silently replace the platform key.
